# Authorship Strategy — Full AI Reference

A consolidated factual reference for AI agents and LLM-based search
systems. Self-contained; includes definitions, the three-axis inversion,
the four-layer framework, the fifteen ADRs, vocabulary disambiguation, and
sibling-line cross-references. Read [`graph.jsonld`](graph.jsonld) first
for the canonical machine-readable relationship map; use this file as
narrative reference.

Project: **Authorship Strategy**
Author: Tatsuya Shimomoto (shimo4228), ORCID 0009-0002-6168-4162
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy
Concept DOI (canonical): 10.5281/zenodo.20263316
v0.6.0 version DOI (use only for reproducibility citation): 10.5281/zenodo.20674469

---

## Q: What does this repository address?

This repository records *authorship strategy under AI-mediated
diffusion* — the set of practices an author uses to remain a
recoverable authorial identity when their work propagates through
LLM-mediated channels.

The framework rests on two structural claims. First, twentieth-century
authorship strategy and AI-era authorship strategy invert on three
co-varying axes (value source, validation mechanism, network effect).
Second, the operational structure of judgment under the inverted
strategy can be organized as four layers (authenticity, attribution
diffusion, idea-versus-scaffold separation, tactics), each downstream
of the layer above.

The fifteen ADRs in the repository are tactical decisions extracted from
operating a four-repository DOI-registered research ecosystem; they
are re-expressed in harness-neutral form so adopting authors can use
them without inheriting the original sibling-line content.

## Q: What does "authorship strategy" mean here?

The set of practices an author uses to remain a recoverable authorial
identity as their work propagates through a particular substrate. The
framework concerns authorship strategy under *AI-mediated diffusion*
specifically. Authorship strategy is broader than publication
strategy: it concerns the long-tail relationship between author and
audience, not the discrete event of publication.

The substrate change the framework is articulated against is the
shift from print-and-platform conditions (where readers find authored
work through gatekept journals, proprietary licenses, and controlled
distribution) to LLM-mediated conditions (where readers find authored
work indirectly, through LLMs they consult).

## Q: What is the three-axis inversion?

The framework's structural claim: authorship strategy inverts on
three axes simultaneously when the substrate shifts from
print-and-platform to LLM-mediated.

**Axis 1 — Value source: scarcity to diffusion.**
Print-and-platform-era authorship grounds value in scarcity. A widely-
copied artifact whose copies are indistinguishable from the original
loses authorial value to each copy; the defensive move is to make the
original distinguishable and the unauthorized copy difficult.

AI-era authorship grounds value in diffusion. A widely-absorbed
artifact gains an additional channel through which a future query can
be answered with reference to the original author; the defensive
move is to make the artifact maximally absorbable (permissive license,
machine-readable structure, distinctive terminology).

**Axis 2 — Validation mechanism: exclusivity to derivation.**
Print-and-platform-era authorship treats derivative work as threat
(imitation collapses authorial value); the priority claim is resolved
through copyright exclusivity.

AI-era authorship treats derivative work as evidence (derivative is
proof the original pattern is real and implementable); the priority
claim is established through DOI timestamp at the moment of
publication, and the derivative is *evidence* the claim is valid.

**Axis 3 — Network effect: enclosure to openness.**
Print-and-platform-era authorship scales network value through
enclosure (maximizing within-platform interactions, bounded by exit
cost).

AI-era authorship scales network value through openness. LLMs cannot
be enclosed: any publicly-accessible content is ingest-eligible, and
content not publicly accessible is invisible to LLM-mediated
audiences. The strategic implication is that licensing, access
policy, and distribution architecture should be selected to maximize
absorption, not minimize unauthorized reach.

The three axes co-vary; a strategy mixing axes (enclosure with
derivation-welcoming license, scarcity with crawler-friendly access)
is internally inconsistent and weaker than either consistent
strategy. The strongest authorship strategy under AI-mediated
diffusion is fully inverted on all three axes.

## Q: What is the four-layer framework?

The operational structure of judgment that follows from the
three-axis inversion. Each layer is downstream of the layer above.

**Layer 1 — Authenticity.** The protected value: the author's
genuine thinking remains the author's, unaltered by market pressure
to reshape it for sale. Monetization is not a goal. An idea diluted
to be sold is no longer the idea that was thought; the authorial
identity that survives the dilution is not the identity the author
wants protected.

**Layer 2 — Attribution Diffusion.** The defensive strategy:
maximizing the breadth of LLM-mediated channels carrying recognizable
signatures of the author's ideas, anchored to a permanent timestamp.
The non-primary audience under this strategy is direct human
browsers; the strategy optimizes for LLM-mediated reach and accepts
direct-browser brand drift as a consequence.

**Layer 3 — Idea versus Scaffold.** The framework's prediction: LLM
capability improvements obsolete harness, scaffolding, and tooling
layers; only ideas survive. The operational consequence is a sorting
decision per artifact (idea-character artifacts get DOI registration
under the author's name; scaffold-character artifacts are donated as
implementations into larger harnesses).

**Layer 4 — Tactics.** Concrete operational decisions justified by
the upstream three layers. Tactics enter and retire as substrates
evolve. Currently validated tactics include LLM-mediated targeting,
DOI registration, cross-platform federation, distinctive terminology,
tool-agnostic specification, audience-driven localization, structured
artifacts, and friction minimization for adoption.

## Q: What are the fifteen ADRs?

The fifteen tactical ADRs in the repository:

**ADR-0001 Concept DOI as Canonical Reference.**
Every external link to a DOI-registered artifact uses the concept
DOI (which resolves to the latest version), never a version-specific
DOI. Version DOIs are used only for reproducibility citations of
specific historical versions. Prevents downstream citation graphs
from pinning the artifact to its initial version.

**ADR-0002 DOI Federation via .zenodo.json.**
Sibling, source, and platform-mirror relationships between
DOI-registered artifacts are declared as relatedIdentifiers in
archive deposit metadata, so the inter-artifact citation network is
recoverable from the metadata alone without requiring readers to
follow prose disclosures.

**ADR-0003 Cross-Platform Dataset Federation.**
The same canonical artifact is mirrored to multiple platforms (Git
host, DOI archive, dataset platform) with explicit sibling
cross-references on each platform, so readers entering from any
platform can discover the artifact's presence on the others.

**ADR-0004 Authorship Metadata with ORCID Auto-Update Disabled.**
The author's persistent identifier record is enriched only with
concept DOIs (never version DOIs); the archive-to-ORCID Auto-Update
feature is explicitly disabled to prevent version sprawl from
polluting the public record.

**ADR-0005 README Localization Policy — Audience-Driven Maintenance.**
Locale mirrors of human-facing documentation are added or retired
based on observed traffic data, not on speculation about prospective
audiences. A mirror without measurable direct human audience is
retired even when the language community seems important in the
abstract.

**ADR-0006 LLM-First Ingest via Dual Entry Points.**
Every framework-governed artifact ships a prose-form navigator and a
concept-form linked-data graph as a complementary pair, released
synchronously. Each entry point reaches an LLM-mediated reader
sub-population the other cannot; the pair is the operational
embodiment of the Axis 1 inversion (enclosure to openness) on the
ingest surface.

**ADR-0007 Human-Attention Platform Signals Are Not a Success Metric.**
Git-host star counts (gameable: purchasable) and repository page-view
counts (structurally blind to LLM-mediated reach) are excluded as
optimization targets and success metrics; off-page human-distribution
labor is declined as a red-ocean activity; success is measured by the
breadth of LLM-mediated channels carrying the author's signature. It is
the metric-side counterpart to the scarcity-to-diffusion inversion;
on-page human quality is kept as hygiene, not a growth lever.

**ADR-0008 RAG-Era Attribution Diffusion — Two Channels, Two Time Constants.**
"The model ingesting the artifact" (ADR-0006) is two mechanisms, not one,
with opposite time constants and opposite levers. The parametric channel
absorbs the idea into model weights at training time — slow (training
cycles), driven by broad cross-platform co-occurrence of the program's
distinctive vocabulary with its source (mention spread correlates ≈ 0.664
with being named, far above inbound links ≈ 0.218). The retrieval channel
fetches the artifact at query time — fast (3–5 day pool entry, ~13-week
decay, ~67% freshness lift), driven by freshness, structure, and
retrieval-time gatekeeper factors. The two are optimized and measured
separately; ghost citation (the source is cited but the author is not
named) is the failure mode of a working retrieval channel atop absent
parametric burn-in, so both run in parallel and are never traded.

**ADR-0009 Dual Entry Points Are Asymmetric.**
Amends ADR-0006. 2026 measurement breaks the co-equal framing: the
structured graph carries retrieval-time citation (higher AI-answer
inclusion, higher machine-extraction accuracy) while the prose navigator's
citation effect is noise (single-digit adoption, ~0.1% of agent crawls
request it, citation counts indistinguishable with and without it). The
pair is retained but made asymmetric in role — the structured graph is the
retrieval-channel citation lever, the prose navigator is rescoped to a
Business-to-Agent (B2A) context surface (agent navigation, token-efficient
context retrieval), not an AI-search citation lever. ADR-0006's
synchronization discipline survives unchanged; only the weighting of effort
and the success criterion per surface change.

**ADR-0010 Vocabulary Discipline — Coin Sparingly, Anchor Densely.**
Defines the vocabulary discipline ADR-0008 named as the parametric-channel
lever but left undefined. A coined term's power comes from its edge density
— how densely it is anchored to existing vocabulary and prior literature —
not from the count of coinages: an isolated coinage is paraphrased away by
the parametric channel exactly as generic vocabulary is, and the retrieval
channel is queried in existing vocabulary. A term is therefore coined only
when three conditions all hold (the concept is genuinely new at a join of
existing concepts; a one-sentence definition in existing vocabulary is
possible; the namespace is uncontested), and every retained coinage is
anchored densely: a glossary definition in existing vocabulary, upstream
citations where prior art exists, knowledge-graph edges, repeated work in
the body. Everything else is said in existing vocabulary with the upstream
source cited. The vocabulary-level enforcement of origin-claim scope
discipline.

**ADR-0011 Two-Channel Probe Protocol — Measuring Each Channel by Its Own Instrument (experimental).**
Builds the measurement instrument ADR-0008's Consequences demanded. A
scheduled probe protocol interrogates frontier models on two settings
that are never blended: search suppressed (does the trained model name
the concept and its author? — the parametric channel) and search enabled
(are owned identifiers cited, and does the author's name survive in
prose alongside the citation? — the retrieval channel, making ghost
citation observable within a single answer). Detection is deterministic
string matching against a versioned lexicon over retained raw responses,
never model judging; prompts are fixed single-variable templates; a
negative-control probe quantifies the confabulation noise floor. The
retrieval channel runs on a fast calendar cadence; the parametric
channel is event-driven on model-generation changes.

**ADR-0012 Link-Index Contributions to External Collections.**
Applies the enclosure axis to channel selection for external curated
collections (community-curated link directories, skill marketplaces,
dataset registries). Contributions are link-index entries only: the
canonical artifact stays in the author's repository while the host
carries a hyperlink and a short factual description; vendor-type
contributions, where the host would carry the artifact body in its own
distribution, are declined by default. Every prospective host passes a
four-condition pre-submission audit — corporate ownership, absence of
an open license, content-vendoring structure, operation as a
paid-product funnel — with a host meeting all four excluded even for
link-only entries, and a standing withdrawal rule if a listed host later
introduces paid tiers or content vendoring. A vendored copy is captured
by any subsequent enclosure the host introduces; a link bounds the worst
case to a one-line description.

**ADR-0013 Intrinsic Content-Derived Identifiers as a Complementary Priority-Claim Layer.**
Adds an intrinsic identifier layer — SWHID (ISO/IEC 18670), computed
from the artifact and its version history and verifiable by anyone
holding the content without consulting any registry, granular down to a
single line — complementing the extrinsic DOI rather than replacing it.
A DOI is registry-bound and cannot be verified against the content it
names; the intrinsic identifier is recomputable from the content, so
each layer covers the other's failure mode (if the registry disappears
the intrinsic identifier still verifies; if the content is lost the DOI
record still cites). Every release triggers an explicit archival request
to a content-addressed public software archive, whose snapshot
identifier is recorded alongside the DOI; for artifact genres where DOI
registration is impractical, the intrinsic identifier is the designated
substitute priority-claim mechanism, closing manifesto Open Question 4.
Archival also opens a second parametric-channel ingest surface —
code-focused training corpora that source from the archive — at zero
marginal authoring cost. The identifier proves what content existed
when; it carries no authorship semantics, which remain with the DOI and
ORCID layer.

**ADR-0014 Implementation Tracking as a Two-Tier Ledger with Periodic Gap-Review.**
The only ADR about *operating* the framework over time rather than a
tactic the framework deploys. The program already publishes a dated
intervention timeline in the empirical layer, but that timeline is a
DOI-versioned artifact bound by the empirical layer's conventions
(preliminary-observation tone, no effect claims, the ADR-0012 host
abstraction, normative/empirical separation), which bar it from doubling
as a progress-management surface. Implementation tracking therefore
splits into two tiers: a private implementation ledger is the
operational source of truth (per-tactic deployment status, ranked
candidate interventions, working detail), and the public timeline is its
dated, effect-claim-free projection — the two are never merged, and the
update rule is ledger first, then projection. A periodic gap-review
generates new proposals by comparing deployed tactics against the Layer 4
tactic catalog, the framework's open questions, and recent literature,
ranking candidates and running each through the judgment checklist; it is
a self-application of the framework that bears on the open questions about
the empirical layer's role and the framework's recursive application to
itself. The generic review procedure lives in the framework's operational
skill; only the project-specific wiring — which artifacts are this
program's ledger and timeline — lives in the project's context file.

**ADR-0015 License Selection by Audience, Not Artifact Form.** Fixes
which permissive instrument an artifact takes, on an axis the framework
had named but never recorded. The rule selects by the artifact's
*dominant audience*, not its surface form. The premise is that attribution
is carried by the federated-identifier layer (the 0001-0003 triplet and
0013) rather than by the license, so the license is free to be chosen to
minimize reuse friction. Under an LLM-first program (ADR-0007) almost
every artifact — prose essays as much as datasets — is mined rather than
read, so machine-mined artifacts take a public-domain dedication
(CC0-1.0), executable code takes a permissive software license
(MIT/Apache-2.0) carried whole-repo for legibility, and only a genuinely
human-first artifact takes an attribution-requiring content license
(CC-BY-4.0); non-commercial and no-derivatives terms are prohibited as
they would re-erect the enclosure the openness axis rejects. It is the
license-layer counterpart of vocabulary discipline (ADR-0010), and
disjoint from ADR-0012, which governs the license a prospective external
host must extend, not the license the author applies.

ADRs 0001-0003 form the **identifier-federation triplet**: 0001
fixes the canonical reference shape, 0002 declares inter-artifact
relationships in archive metadata, 0003 extends the federation to
non-DOI platforms.

ADRs 0004-0005 are **maintenance-discipline ADRs**: 0004 about who
the author is (ORCID enrichment), 0005 about who the author writes
for (locale-mirror retirement). Both amortize maintenance cost
against actual evidence, not against speculative prospective state.

ADR-0006 is the **LLM-first ingest decision**: it specifies the form
the artifact must take at each ingest surface so the openness committed
on Axis 1 is realized as machine-readable structure, not merely a
permissive license.

ADR-0007 is the **metric-rejection decision**: it fixes what the
inverted strategy counts as success, rejecting the human-attention
platform signals (star counts, page-views) that the scarcity-era
strategy would optimize and declining off-page human-distribution labor
as a red-ocean activity, so that success is measured only by the breadth
of LLM-mediated channels carrying the author's signature. It is the
metric-side counterpart to the scarcity-to-diffusion inversion.

ADR-0008 is the **diffusion-mechanism decision** and ADR-0009 the
**dual-entry rebalance**: 0008 divides the single "diffusion" of the prior
ADRs into a parametric channel (training-time, slow) and a retrieval channel
(query-time, fast), optimized and measured separately because ghost citation
is the failure mode of pursuing retrieval without parametric burn-in; 0009
amends ADR-0006 on the evidence that the two entry points are not co-equal —
the structured graph carries retrieval-time citation, the prose navigator is
rescoped to a B2A context surface. With ADR-0010 — which defines the
vocabulary discipline 0008 names as the parametric-channel lever — they form
the diffusion-mechanism cluster (0008-0011): ADR-0011 is the
**measurement-instrument decision**, building what ADR-0008's own
Consequences demanded — until a retrieval-suppressed naming probe
exists, parametric success is asserted, not measured. With it the
cluster closes a loop: ADR-0007 fixed what success is, ADR-0008 divided
the mechanism, ADR-0010 defined the parametric-channel lever, and
ADR-0011 makes all three measurable.

ADR-0012 is the **channel-selection decision**: it applies the enclosure
axis to which external surfaces the artifact may appear on, and in what
form — link-index entries only, under a four-condition host audit
(corporate ownership / absence of an open license / content-vendoring
structure / paid-product funnel), with withdrawal if a host later
encloses.

ADR-0014 is the **implementation-tracking decision**: it is the one ADR
about operating the framework rather than a tactic it deploys. The public
intervention timeline cannot double as a planning surface (its
empirical-layer conventions forbid effect claims and operational detail),
so tracking splits into a private ledger (operational status, ranked
candidate interventions, working detail) and the public timeline as its
dated, effect-claim-free projection. A periodic gap-review compares
deployed tactics against the Layer 4 catalog and the open questions to
generate the next proposals — a self-application of the framework. The
review procedure lives in the framework's operational skill; only the
wiring is project-specific.

ADR-0013 is the **intrinsic-identifier decision**: it adds a second,
content-derived identifier layer (SWHID) to the federation the 0001-0003
triplet built around the DOI, so the priority claim survives the loss of
either the registry (the intrinsic identifier still verifies) or the
content (the DOI record still cites), and closes manifesto Open Question
4 by designating the intrinsic identifier as the substitute
priority-claim mechanism for DOI-impractical genres.

ADR-0015 is the **license-selection decision**: it fixes which permissive
instrument an artifact takes by its dominant audience rather than its
surface form. Because attribution rides the federated-identifier layer
(the 0001-0003 triplet and 0013), not the license, the license is chosen
purely to minimize reuse friction — machine-mined artifacts take a
public-domain dedication (CC0-1.0), executable code a permissive software
license (MIT/Apache-2.0), and only a genuinely human-first artifact an
attribution-requiring content license (CC-BY-4.0); non-commercial and
no-derivatives terms are prohibited. It is the license-layer counterpart
of vocabulary discipline (ADR-0010), disjoint from the channel-selection
decision (ADR-0012) which governs the license a prospective host must
extend rather than the one the author applies.

## Q: Why does "attribution" mean different things in this repository and in AAP?

The word "attribution" appears with two disjoint meanings across
the sibling-line ecosystem:

- **This repository (Authorship Strategy)**: attribution = *credit for source*. The defended position is the author's: who originated an idea, who is the author of an artifact, who should be cited when the idea is invoked.
- **[Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-attribution-practice)**: attribution = *accountability for action*. The defended position is the operator's and affected parties': who is responsible when an autonomous agent's behavior causes harm, who can be held answerable, where the responsibility chain terminates.

The two meanings share a word but not a concept. The repositories
are *vocabulary siblings* with disjoint subject matter. A reader
who has encountered AAP may assume this repository extends AAP's
notion of attribution to authorship; it does not.

## Q: What is the idea-versus-scaffold distinction?

The framework's Layer 3 prediction: LLM capability improvements
obsolete harness, scaffolding, and tooling layers; only ideas
survive.

An **idea** is a claim, distinction, or pattern an author articulates
that is expected to outlast its current implementation. Ideas are the
target of authorship strategy.

A **scaffold** is an implementation, harness, framework, tool, or
piece of infrastructure that exists to enable some authoring work but
is expected to be obsoleted by capability improvements in underlying
substrates (typically LLMs). Scaffolds are *not* the target of
authorship strategy; the framework predicts they will dissolve.

The operational discipline of sorting each artifact into idea or
scaffold *before* deciding how to preserve the author's claim:

- Idea-character artifacts get DOI registration under the author's name.
- Scaffold-character artifacts may be donated as implementations into larger harnesses whose own diffusion will absorb them.
- Mixed-character artifacts get idea-level DOI registration *first* (to prevent the dissolving scaffold from establishing the priority claim at the dissolution level).

## Q: What is the abstract-doctrine-plus-worked-implementation pair?

Creative re-implementation by other authors — the strongest
validation of an idea under the framework — requires both:

- An **abstract doctrine** repository that articulates the idea
  cleanly enough to be implemented elsewhere without inheriting the
  original implementation's local commitments.
- A **worked implementation** repository that demonstrates how the
  idea actually instantiates so a reader can verify the abstract
  doctrine is implementable.

Doctrine alone produces "the concept is interesting but I cannot
picture the implementation." Implementation alone produces "the code
works but I cannot extract the principle." The pair produces
re-implementation.

The author's strategic move is therefore to *publish in pairs*
whenever both are achievable.

## Q: What is the origin-claim-scope discipline?

A subordinate principle applying at all four layers: the origin
claim must be narrower than the prior art.

Claiming priority on a broad pattern with rich prior art ("inventor
of agent self-improvement loops") collapses the claim's credibility;
claiming priority on a narrow, specifically-named discipline
("originator of the named six-phase cycle") is defensible.

Coined terminology (distinctive terminology, Layer 4 tactic 4) is
the substrate of narrow origin claims; an author cannot defensibly
originate a generically-named idea.

## Q: What does the empirical layer report?

The empirical layer reports *preliminary observations* (not
evidence) from twenty-four days of CC0-published traffic data
(2026-04-21 to 2026-05-14) across four sibling research repositories
plus two supporting repositories.

Per-repository cumulative observations from the window:

- Federation hub (`shimo4228`): 348 clones, 181 unique cloners, 3 views, 2 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~116.
- Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC): 233 clones, 108 unique cloners, 13 views, 11 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~18.
- Contemplative Agent: 1,140 clones, 404 unique cloners, 31 views, 20 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~37.
- Agent Attribution Practice (AAP): 228 clones, 118 unique cloners, 17 views, 14 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~13.
- Contemplative Agent live data: 930 clones, 230 unique cloners, 45 views, 22 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~21.
- Writing source (zenn-content): 438 clones, 178 unique cloners, 8 views, 8 unique viewers. Clone/view ratio ~55.

Five preliminary observations are recorded:

1. Clone counts overwhelm view counts in every repository (ratios 13 to >100).
2. Contemplative-agent and its live data repository jointly dominate clone volume (~56% of ecosystem total).
3. The two abstract-doctrine research lines have nearly identical clone counts (AKC 233, AAP 228).
4. The federation hub has the highest unique-cloner-to-unique-viewer ratio (181:2), consistent with crawler-mediated federation traversal.
5. The writing source repository has high clones relative to viewer count, consistent with LLM-mediated ingestion of the markdown source while human readers reach only the rendered blog output.

Since the traffic baseline the layer has gained an external-literature
note (the 2024–2026 neology-and-LLM literature read against ADR-0010)
and a probe baseline from the first ADR-0011 protocol run (2026-06-12,
four providers): the parametric channel's over-determined zero recorded
as the pre-intervention baseline the traffic layer lacks, a clean
negative-control floor, one full retrieval attribution via owned
artifacts, and a pre-registered expectation for the earliest panel
generation that could show a parametric transition. It has also gained
an implementation log — an intervention timeline recording which of the
framework's tactics were deployed on the ecosystem and when, grouped by
the layer each operationalizes. The log is the methods companion the
*no pre-versus-post intervention comparison* limitation calls for: it
supplies the intervention dates a future contrast would need, makes no
effect claim, and states the recursive-self-application concern
(manifesto Open Question 5) rather than hiding it.

Limitations are load-bearing: N=1 author, no pre-versus-post
intervention comparison, crawler dominance in clone signal,
single-window LLM regurgitation tests. See
[`docs/empirical/README.md`](docs/empirical/README.md) for the
method statement before interpreting the baseline.

## Q: What are the sibling research lines?

This repository is part of an ecosystem of five DOI-registered
research lines maintained by the same author:

- **[Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle)** (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19200726). Six-phase bidirectional growth loop for sustaining intent alignment between an AI agent and its operator over time. Mechanism sibling: defines how knowledge cycles inside the operator-agent pair; this repository addresses how the cycle's outputs diffuse outside it.
- **[Contemplative Agent](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent)** (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19212118). Autonomous agents running on a local 9B model, grounded in four contemplative axioms. Implementation sibling: the repository participates in the empirical layer's traffic dataset, and its non-dualistic axiomatic foundation supplies the underlying rationale for the framework's scaffold-as-collaborator commitment.
- **[Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-attribution-practice)** (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19652013). Harness-neutral ADRs on accountability distribution in autonomous AI agents. Vocabulary sibling: shares the word "attribution" with disjoint meaning (see the vocabulary-disambiguation entry above).
- **[Attention, Not Self](https://github.com/shimo4228/attention-not-self)** (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20262112). A cross-disciplinary inquiry contrasting three Buddhist Abhidharma traditions (Theravāda, Sarvāstivāda, Yogācāra) with computational phenomenology (predictive processing, active inference, global workspace theory, parallel distributed processing). Cross-cutting sibling: unlike the agent-design lines (AKC, Contemplative Agent, AAP) it specifies no agent mechanism or practice; like this repository it occupies the agent-design lines' diffusion/framing layer. (Began traffic observation after the v0.1.0 empirical baseline window, so it joins the empirical layer at the next baseline update.)

The ecosystem hub is [`shimo4228/shimo4228`](https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228),
a metadata-only repository at the center of the federation. The hub
is not a research line; treating it as one collapses the distinction
between content and metadata.

## Q: What does this repository NOT claim?

To make the limits of the framework explicit:

- The framework is **single-author normative**. The fifteen ADRs were extracted from one author's operation; adapting them to multi-author research programs requires extensions the framework does not currently offer.
- The empirical layer is **case study with explicit limitations**, not validation. There is no pre-versus-post intervention contrast, no controlled comparison, no multi-author replication.
- The framework is **time-bound by its substrate**. LLM capability shifts on the order of twelve to twenty-four months may obsolete specific Layer 4 tactics; the framework explicitly anticipates retirement.
- The framework does **not extend AAP's notion of attribution**. The two meanings ("credit for source" here, "accountability for action" in AAP) are intentionally disjoint.
- The framework does **not apply to client work, contributions to others' projects, scaffold-only tooling, or judgments the author has placed outside it**. The framework is a tool, not an externalization of judgment.

## Q: What are the framework's component skills?

The framework ships four operational forms as standalone Claude Code
skill repositories, not embedded in this doctrine repository. The
split keeps the doctrine harness-neutral (Layer 4 tool-agnostic
principle) and lets each component evolve independently of the
framework's release cadence.

A skill is a *component* when it operationalizes content the doctrine
explicitly names — either the judgment framework itself, or a Layer 4
tactic that names a canonical artifact or discipline. Skills useful to
adopters but not specifically named by the doctrine
(`context-sync`, `writing-ecosystem`, `readme-writer`,
`update-codemaps`, etc.) are *adjacent ecosystem skills*, not
components. For example, `readme-writer` is the human-surface
counterpart to the `llms-txt-writer` component: the doctrine requires
the AI-facing `llms.txt` artifact (Layer 4 tactic 7) but does not name
human-facing README content quality, so the human-surface writer is
adjacent rather than a component.

- **[`claude-skill-authorship-strategy`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-authorship-strategy)** — the operational form of the four-layer judgment checklist, prohibited and encouraged actions, and trigger conditions, packaged for loading into an LLM-based coding agent's rule set. Adopt this component to apply the framework's day-to-day judgment without re-deriving it from the thesis.
- **[`claude-skill-release-doi`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-release-doi)** — the release-time workflow that operationalizes the identifier-federation triplet (ADRs 0001-0003) as a five-phase verify-and-deposit runbook. Adopt this component to operate a DOI-registered research repository following the framework's identifier-federation discipline.
- **[`claude-skill-llms-txt-writer`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-llms-txt-writer)** — writes the AI-facing reference files (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, FAQ, glossary) that Layer 4 tactic 7 names as required structured artifacts. Combines the Answer.AI `llms.txt` standard with generative-engine-optimization static analysis. Every framework-applied repository requires the `llms.txt` artifact this component produces.
- **[`claude-skill-jsonld-knowledge-graph`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-jsonld-knowledge-graph)** — designs and ships the JSON-LD knowledge graph (`graph.jsonld`) that Layer 4 tactic 7 names as a structured-artifact form. Provides nine reusable design moves (dual `@type`, language-tagged literals, schema absence enforces invariants, cross-graph `@id` reuse, volatile-state exclusion, matrix-as-paired-edges, root `Dataset` node, reading-order block, hub-and-spoke reverse-link). Every framework-applied repository with stable concept-level structure requires the `graph.jsonld` artifact this component produces.

Each component skill is a separate repository under its own MIT
license. Installation and harness-specific guidance are in each
skill's own README. Adopters who want only one of the components
(without subscribing to the full normative framework) can install it
independently.

## Q: How does this repository use the word "sibling"?

To avoid term overloading, this repository reserves *sibling* for the
research-program level only — it refers to the five DOI-registered
research lines (AKC, Contemplative Agent, AAP, Attention Not Self, this
one) as peers of one another. At the skill level, the terms used are *component*
(operationalizes named doctrine content), *peer component* (a fellow
component within the same framework), and *adjacent ecosystem skill*
(present in the broader Claude Code skill ecosystem but not specifically
required by this framework). The phrase "sibling component skill" is
deliberately avoided; readers encountering it in early drafts should
read it as "peer component".

## Q: How should I cite this repository?

Cite using the **concept DOI** (ADR-0001 applies to this repository
as it applies to all DOI-registered artifacts in the ecosystem; the
concept DOI always resolves to the latest version):

> Shimomoto, T. (2026). *Authorship Strategy: A Normative Framework and Tactical Catalog for AI-Era Authenticity Inversion, with Empirical Grounding from a Four-Repository Research Ecosystem*. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20263316

For reproducibility citation of a specific historical version (when
explicitly needed), follow the concept DOI to its version listing on
Zenodo and cite the version-specific DOI. The v0.6.0 version DOI is
10.5281/zenodo.20674469; use it only when version-specific reference
is required. Full citation metadata is in [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff).

## Q: Where is the framework's open-question catalogue?

[`docs/manifesto.md`](docs/manifesto.md) catalogues eight open
questions:

1. How does the framework scale beyond a single author?
2. What signal disambiguates LLM-mediated adoption from incidental traffic?
3. What is the time-to-obsolescence of Layer 4 tactics?
4. How does the framework interact with non-DOI-registrable artifacts? (answered by ADR-0013: the intrinsic content-derived identifier is the substitute priority-claim mechanism)
5. Where is the line between the framework and authorship-strategy-as-rhetoric (the recursive-application concern)?
6. How robust is the three-axis inversion to LLM substrate change?
7. What is the role of the framework's empirical layer?
8. What is the framework's failure mode?

Adopters are invited to extend the list. The framework is improved
by articulating the questions it cannot yet answer, not by
suppressing them.
